title: Hybrid retention orchestrator for KV cache with prefix-isolation correctness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid KV cache retention/orchestration layer that composes LRU, TTL, and prefix-isolation policies into a single correctness-preserving eviction executor. This ticket covers the API surface, deterministic invariants, memory accounting, and a safe rollout plan for runtime-1.20.
background: We operate a GPU-resident KV cache to accelerate autoregressive generation across many concurrent sessions. Current heuristics mix LRU and TTL with ad-hoc prefix heuristics; multiple incidents show intermittent prefix-bleed (stale KV for other prefixes) and non-deterministic memory pressure spikes during busy continuous-batching workloads. We need a formal orchestrator that gives application-level correctness guarantees (no prefix contamination, bounded staleness per prefix) while meeting latency and GPU memory targets.
goal: Provide a hybrid eviction orchestrator that: 1) enforces prefix isolation invariants, 2) guarantees bounded staleness for pinned prefixes (TTL windows), 3) prevents atomicity gaps during concurrent reclamation and prefetch, and 4) exposes knobs for cost/latency tradeoffs to autoscaling and batching layers.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and platform leads
Implementation in runtime-1.20 branch with feature gate `kv.hybrid_orchestrator`
Unit & integration tests proving: prefix isolation (no cross-prefix KV reuse), TTL bounds honored within +/- 1 request boundary, and memory accounting under synthetic workloads
Benchmarks vs baseline: <=5% median token latency increase at same QPS, and >=20% reduction in eviction-triggered tail latency spikes
Canary rollout plan documented and smoke checks defined (telemetry queries and dashboards)
proposed_solution: Introduce a modular orchestrator that composes three logical layers: (A) memory accounting and reservation tokens per request cohort, (B) prefix affinity fencing (logical 'ownership lease' per prefix segment), and (C) eviction executor that applies policy prioritized buckets: pinned -> TTL -> LRU within prefix windows. Key mechanics: 1) each prefix append increments a monotonic epoch and obtains a soft reservation token; 2) reclamation marks a prefix fence and collects candidates respecting KV sequence numbers to avoid mid-query invalidation; 3) reclamation is cooperative with batch scheduler: eviction runs at controlled windows between micro-batches to avoid KV churn during hot loops. The orchestrator exposes a small API to autoscaler and batcher: ReserveMemory(request_id, estimated_tokens), ReleaseMemory(request_id), and FencePrefix(prefix_id, mode).
implementation_tasks: API: add reservation and fence primitives to kv_store interface (C++ runtime)
Memory Accounting: implement per-cohort accounting with atomic counters and watermark thresholds
Prefix Fence: implement lightweight prefix-lease metadata and integrate with caching index
Eviction Executor: implement bucketed collector honoring pinned/TTL/LRU ordering and sequence-number safety checks
Testing harness: extend existing cache_fuzzer to simulate continuous batching, multi-prefix workloads, TTL expiries and concurrent prefetch
Telemetry: add metrics for lease ops, reservation failures, eviction reasons, reclaimed bytes by prefix
Rolling feature-flagged rollout: cluster agent changes + runtime flag `kv.hybrid_orchestrator`
tradeoffs: The hybrid orchestrator introduces additional per-request accounting and fence metadata which increases CPU overhead and a few bytes of GPU metadata per prefix. We trade a small CPU/memory tax for stronger correctness and reduced tail latency. Strict prefix-isolation can reduce cache reuse across prefixes, potentially increasing token cost in some workloads; the orchestrator will allow a 'prefix-relax' mode to relax fences for low-importance workloads. There is complexity in integrating with the continuous-batching runtime; to mitigate risk we will gate with a feature flag and validate with canaries.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for reservation/fence lifecycles and eviction ordering. 2) Integration tests with the runtime batcher: deterministic scenarios where eviction would previously cause stale KV reads. 3) End-to-end load tests with our benchmark cluster: long-tail generation sessions across 100k prefixes and mixed TTLs. 4) Chaos tests: kill evictor mid-run, simulate OOM triggers, validate no cross-prefix contamination post-restart. Telemetry assertions will be used for canary validation.
metrics_and_alerts: kv.cross_prefix_hits (should be zero in strict mode)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: increased CPU contention in headroom-critical hosts -> Mitigation: sampling-based eviction and optional lightweight mode
Risk: cache efficiency regressions for multi-tenant low-traffic prefixes -> Mitigation: prefix-relax policy and histogram-based auto-tuning
Risk: rollout-induced partial invalidations -> Mitigation: sequence-number driven atomic fence, integration tests and canary windows
rollout_plan: Feature-gated on `kv.hybrid_orchestrator`. Phase 1: internal dev cluster (2 weeks) with synthetic load. Phase 2: 10% canary in us-east with telemetry smoke checks (2 weeks). Phase 3: 50% with targeted clients disabled if reservation failures exceed 0.5% for 30 minutes. Full rollout after 4 weeks of stable telemetry.
